title: PortPilot Run State
description: Owned exclusively by the winport orchestrator. The audit trail of a single port: which stage ran, which gate was checked, what it decided, and why work was routed where it was. No specialist agent may write this file - it is the record of the decisions made ABOUT them. Its purpose is that a human can reconstruct, months later, exactly why a port was accepted or sent back.

maxReviewRounds.description: The loop budget. Exceeding it means stopping and reporting honestly, not lowering the bar until something passes.

status.description: blocked-external exists because the first real run needed it: the port was correct and the review was correct, but a hard gate required hardware the environment did not have. Neither 'passed' nor 'failed' is honest there - one overstates what was proven, the other understates what was achieved. A run may only end blocked-external if the outstanding gate is provably unactionable by any agent, and blockedBy must say what a human needs in order to close it.

blockedBy.description: Required when status is blocked-external. What is missing, and what would resolve it.

history.description: Append-only. Failed gates are never deleted - a run that shows no failures either did nothing interesting or is hiding something.

check.description: Required on gate entries: what was actually checked, phrased so a reader can re-run it.
